narrative.text: Hi, I'm Teemo. I've finished analysing this patient's record.
The estimated chance of being readmitted within 30 days is 20 percent. That is a high risk.
It's about 1.8 times the hospital average of 11 percent. It's higher than 88 percent of the patients I was tested on.
In testing, about 25 out of 100 patients in this high risk group really did come back within a month.
The biggest factor raising the risk is hospital visit history: 3 inpatient stays, no ER visits, no outpatient visits.
Next comes admitting specialty: not recorded.
On the positive side, diabetes medication, none and discharge destination, home help lower the risk.
Nurse call within 72 hours. Enroll the patient in a transitional-care phone follow-up after discharge.
Follow-up visit within 7 days. Book the appointment before the patient leaves the ward.
Assign a care coordinator. Repeated recent visits — review why and build one shared care plan.
Medication reconciliation. Pharmacist review of every medication and dose change before discharge.
Remember, I'm a decision-support tool. The care team always makes the final call. Take care!
